- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, expect overshoot or overconfidence; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- If recent sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecast is rising, it’s likely a lag error — correct by reducing forecast slope by 0.5–1.0 units per day.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts — cap forecast increase to 2–3% per day for next 3–5 days.
- When official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model tends to underreact — add 1–3% to forecast mean for next 7–10 days.
- If model forecast is trending upward but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5 units per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model, check sentiment history for recent volatility — if sentiment is mixed or negative, apply a 5–10% downward bias to next forecast.
